main_body: Shrine hall: a large green tiled hip roof with a ridge cap and gold finials, over a cream plaster wall with red posts, a dark lattice double door, and a stone base.
top_band: At x=48: the gold finials (rows 0-3) sit on a light green ridge cap (rows 4-9, L 168 to 47). Below it the tile slope runs rows 10-41 (L 138/112/66 with tile highlights). A light edge at rows 42-43 closes the slope, then the red lintel beam follows at rows 44-46.
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above and in front, with a ridge cap and a pale eave edge at rows 42-43. A red lintel beam sits directly under that edge as an eave shadow. Below it is a distinct vertical wall face with posts, a lattice door set darker inside the frame, and a stone base. This is the same structure as the Beodeul house references, so it reads as a correct 3/4 building. The roof slope is the top surface and the wall is the front face.

style.evidence: The roof has about 6 green steps, but they form a regular grid of identical tile columns with no per-tile scallops or variation. The cream wall is almost one flat colour with only sparse speckle. The black-purple outline pixels at the roof edge and tips are neutral: 83% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7-9% on both references, which gives the sticker look. Only 32 distinct colours, against 66 and 185 on the references, so it is clearly poorer in colour variety. The median of 11 colours per tile only matches the stone reference. The roof is well constructed, but the outline and the flat wall make it thinner than the Beodeul pieces.
